Definition: from Ἀδρία (a place near its shore); the Adriatic sea (including the Ionian):--Adria.
BiblicalUsage: Adrias is the Adriatic Sea — the stretch of water where Paul's ship was driven up and down in the storm, fourteen nights without seeing sun or stars, before it wrecked on Malta. Luke names the sea once, at the darkest point of the voyage, when the sailors suspected they were nearing land; the place itself is covered in the Biblical Places collection.
TheologicalSignificance: There is no doctrine in a sea's name, and I won't pretend there is. What the storm on the Adrias does show is that God's promise to Paul held through fourteen nights of darkness — the ship would be lost, but not one life.
